perspective:
From Gloria Bangura’s perspective:

- She is an administrative assistant at a large event planning company, where Donald works part-time as a bartender during events.
- Over several company events, she noticed that Donald seemed distracted and lacked enthusiasm while serving drinks.
- She initiated a conversation with him, telling him she noticed he seemed “a bit off” and asking if everything was okay with the job.
- Donald told her he was “just not as into it as I used to be” and that it felt “kind of repetitive.”
- After thinking about it, she suggested to Donald that sometimes work dissatisfaction might be connected to larger personal issues, and asked if he had considered talking to a professional.
- Donald said he hadn’t considered that and wasn’t sure if it would help.
- She sensed a possible change in Donald’s behavior toward her and worried that he might have resented her suggestion or felt she overstepped.
- She apologized to Donald, saying she only wanted to help because she cared and didn’t mean to make assumptions.
- Donald told her it was okay; he admitted he was “a bit taken aback at first” but knew she meant well, and said it was “a lot to process.”
- Feeling relieved that the tension had eased, she invited Donald to collaborate on a new project, telling him she thought it could use his creative input.
- Donald accepted, saying he appreciated it and would like to be more involved.
- After working together on the project, she observed Donald’s significant contributions and renewed enthusiasm.
- During a team meeting, she publicly acknowledged Donald’s hard work, saying his efforts were crucial to the project’s success.
- Donald thanked her, said it meant a lot to him, and told her it felt great to be appreciated.
